advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the CWD->repo-root resolution change for replay/ledger output paths is intended and does not relocate artifacts for existing invocations run from a subdirectory.
evidence: Old: `_DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = Path("docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay")` and `_DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR = Path("docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/cache")` — CWD-relative.
New: `evals_corpus_root` returns `_root_config.repo_root(repo_root) / candidate` for a relative value (config_readers.py, `return _root_config.repo_root(repo_root) / candidate`).
`repo_root()` resolves `explicit > REBAR_ROOT > git toplevel of CWD` (per _read_llm_file_table docstring, config_readers.py:49), which is not the process CWD in the general case.
advisory.finding: Replay/ledger output paths changed from CWD-relative (`Path("docs/experiments/...")`) to repo-root-relative resolution via `evals_corpus_root` -> `_root_config.repo_root(repo_root)`. The commit claims 'no behaviour change', but when the harness is invoked from a subdirectory (CWD != repo root) the prior literals resolved against CWD whereas the new code resolves against the git toplevel/REBAR_ROOT, so artifact locations can differ for the same invocation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_no_hard_coded_roots with a behavioral assertion that the resolved cache/out/ledger defaults come from the config layer (e.g. assert replay_dir()/default_ledger_path() drive the __main__ defaults) rather than grepping src for 'docs/experiments'.
evidence: tests/unit/evals/test_evals_corpus_root.py:101-108 — `git grep -n docs/experiments -- src/rebar/llm/evals ... assert [line.split(":")[0] for line in hits] == ["src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py"]`
The grep target is executable source under test, not a non-executable instruction artifact, so the Rule-5 structural-grep exception does not apply.
The equal-to-single-file assertion breaks on a rename of corpus.py or any new comment mentioning the string, with no observable behavior change (Rule-4 refactoring violation).
advisory.finding: test_no_hard_coded_roots greps the SOURCE CODE under test (src/rebar/llm/evals) for the literal 'docs/experiments' and asserts the exact set of matching files. This is a source-grep change-detector, not a behavior assertion: it would break on a behavior-preserving change (renaming corpus.py, rewording its docstring, or any new unrelated comment that mentions docs/experiments) without any observable-behavior change, and it tests the implementation text rather than exercising the resolution code path.
